newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse postpones trading range revision.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse postpones trading range revision.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Thailand has postponed the introduction of the 30 percent daily trading range limit on common shares originally planned for August 1, a spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"I can confirm the exchange has postponed its introduction of the rule," she said.
Common shares are currently allowed to move in a 10 percent daily range from the previous day's close.
No reasons for the decision and no date for the rules introduction has been given.
Officials from the Stock Exchange and the Securities Exchange Commission met with a parliamentary panel on Tuesday to discuss the measure's introduction.
Broker members of the exchange voted earlier this month to widen the trading band. The decision was made just after the baht was floated on July 2.
After the baht float many stocks hit their 10 percent daily ceilings early in the trading day and many orders could not be completed. The widening was meant to free up trading and add liquidity.
But some have criticised the timing of the measure, saying it could bring more volatility to the market just as Thailand is struggling to handle a severe economic crisis.
"With a 30 percent limit some stocks are going to overshoot either up or down. To introduce it at this time might seem like a brave decision," said one foreign trader.
